title: Sebastian and the Summer
premise: Ines Winterbourne, a cellist whose hands froze mid-concert in front of a thousand people, retreats to her late grandmother's vineyard intending to sell it and disappear. But the deed inexplicably names Sebastian Alarcón—the estranged son of the man her grandmother loved and lost—as co-owner, and he arrives with his own grief and his own claim. As they fight over the orchard through one long summer of repairs and near-harvests, Ines learns the deed was her grandmother's deliberate act: a forced inheritance meant to make two families finish what they abandoned. When developers circle and the harvest deadline looms, Ines must choose between selling her half to escape and staying to keep what she never knew she wanted; she stays, plays again at the harvest festival, and lets Sebastian stay after the last train leaves.
about_author: A. M. Quintana is the pen name of a former orchestral librarian who spent a decade cataloguing other people's music before writing her own stories. She lives near an old orchard she refuses to sell, and this is her second novel.

chapters.title: The Deed That Wouldn't Die
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Fresh from her catastrophic final performance, Ines arrives at Winterbourne Orchard intending to sign it away within a week. The county clerk's office reveals two names on the deed—hers and Sebastian Alarcón's—and no legal way to separate them quickly. Emotional beat: cold control cracking into disbelief as her clean exit plan dies on a bureaucratic technicality.

chapters.title: A Stranger with Keys
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian arrives with his father's old keys and a lawyer's letter, equally furious about the shared inheritance. Their first meeting is a standoff in the overgrown driveway, each convinced the other forged their way onto the deed. Emotional beat: mutual suspicion sharpened by an unwanted, immediate recognition of something familiar in each other.

chapters.title: Letters in the Root Cellar
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Clearing the house for sale, Ines finds decades of letters between her grandmother and Sebastian's father—love letters that stop abruptly in 1979. She hides them from Sebastian while reading them nightly. Emotional beat: grief for a grandmother she thought she knew, and the first tremor of doubt about which family was wronged.

chapters.title: The Broken Trellis
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A storm collapses the trellis holding the oldest vines; without repairs before harvest, the crop—and any sale value—is ruined. Sebastian, a carpenter by trade, starts fixing it alone. Ines appears with tools and no explanation. Emotional beat: grudging cooperation becoming rhythm, two bodies working in wordless sync neither will acknowledge.

chapters.title: What the Heart Trains For
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A local string quartet begs Ines to play at the harvest festival; she refuses, hands shaking at the mere suggestion. Later, caught off guard, she plays a fragment for Sebastian in the barn—and doesn't freeze. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration intertwined, the terrifying discovery that her hands work when he's listening.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A developer offers each of them enough money to walk away clean—if both sign. Sebastian, drowning in his own debts, wants to accept but hesitates when he sees Ines's face. He says nothing about the offer for three days. Emotional beat: guilt curdling into secrecy, duty to his dead father warring against a want he can't name.

chapters.title: Nineteen Seventy-Nine
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines finally shows Sebastian the letters; together they learn their grandparents separated because Ines's grandmother chose the vineyard over eloping, and his father never forgave her—or himself. The deed was her last letter: a plea for the grandchildren to finish the sentence. Emotional beat: inherited anger dissolving into shared sorrow, and the first honest touch.

chapters.title: Sign or Stay
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The developer's deadline forces the truth out; Ines feels betrayed by his silence and signs nothing, telling him to take the money and go. He packs, and the chapter ends with him standing at the empty train platform as the last train of the season departs without him. Emotional beat: heartbreak chosen deliberately—he misses the train on purpose and can't yet say why.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Harvest day arrives with the developer circling and the trellis-heavy vines heavy with fruit. Ines, choosing justice outside any contract, tears up her half of the sale agreement and picks grapes beside Sebastian until dark. Emotional beat: the climax—her hands steady in the vines, her heart uncontainable, choosing the orchard and the man over the exit she planned.

chapters.title: After the Last Train
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. At the harvest festival, Ines performs publicly for the first time since her collapse, playing her grandmother's favorite piece to a full town square. Afterward, she finds Sebastian waiting where the last train would leave, and asks him to stay—not for the deed, but for himself. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; love accepted not as surrender but as inheritance, freely kept.
